checks.what: The Northern Yuan page supports it: 'In 1375, Naghachu, a Mongol official of Biligtu Khan in Liaoyang province invaded Liaodong' and 'Although he continued to hold southern Manchuria, Naghachu eventually surrendered to the Ming dynasty in 1387-88'. Liaoning plus Jilin resolves to 1,897 cells (about 480,000 km2, 119-131 E, 38.8-46.3 N). That is a fair reading of 'southern Manchuria', and the Ming dossier's ledger/22 also calls it 'Naghachu's country'. The trial moves 1,881 cells that nobody held to the Northern Yuan in 1375 and takes nothing from Goryeo or any other state. The Ming dossier's 1387-88 events and events/1 hand the land on, so later years are not broken. The years 1368-74 stay unheld because the page dates only 1375.

The Naghachu page says 'in 1387 the Ming sent a military campaign to attack Naghachu and forced his surrender', and the Northern Yuan page gives '1387-88'. 1388 falls inside the page range. It also matches the Ming dossier's own contest_end of 1388 and the annexation of the Liaodong peninsula, which the Hongwu page puts after the 1388 campaign. In the trial the event moves the 365 Liaoning cells outside the peninsula in 1388, so all 1,896 cells are Ming by 1388. Dating it 1387 would fit the Naghachu page a little better but would bring the peninsula forward a year; I left it.

The page says 'Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi remained in Theodore's hands until 11 June 1394, when he ceded them to Venice'. Year, month, parties and land all match. The Argolid region is 7 cells, about 1,770 km2 at 22.6-23.4 E, and runs from the Argos plain to the Thermisi end of the peninsula. The 'minus Corinth 22 km' part removes nothing but is harmless. The note is wrong to suggest the cession was lost: despotate-of-the-morea ledger/2 (loss to Venice, June 1394, a 20 km disc at Argos) already moved 5 cells in the published draft. With this gain in place the compiler skips that loss as a paired event, so 1394 now moves 3 cells, the Argolid part. The other 2 disc cells, on the Arcadian and Nemean side west and north-west of Argos, become unheld at the Morea's 1394 keyframe, one year earlier than in the published draft. The net effect is neutral to slightly better.

The Colhuacan (altepetl) page says 'in 1377 Azcapotzalco subdued Culhuacan in large part with Aztec troops', and the Colhuacan disambiguation page puts Pueblo Culhuacan in 'the Iztapalapa borough of modern Mexico City'. The note states the date conflict with the dossier's 1385. The Mexico City admin-1 stand-in is 4 cells: Culhuacan's cell at 19.29 N 99.16 W, plus Xochimilco-Milpa Alta, Tlalpan-Ajusco and the cell Azcapotzalco shares with Tenochtitlan. That is wider than Colhuacan, but no finer named spec exists, so I accept it. The note was wrong to say Tenochtitlan's cells stay its own. Since the Tlatelolco split of 1337 (tenochtitlan ledger/1) the shared Mexico City cell has had no owner, so the trial moves all 4 cells from nobody to Azcapotzalco. That is still better than the published draft, where Azcapotzalco holds no land from 1326.

checks.what: The Hongwu page says the Ming reached Dadu 'in early September' 1368 and 'The Yuan emperor Toghon Temur fled north to Shangdu'. In 1370 he was forced 'to retreat further north to Yingchang', and 'In June, Li conquered Yingchang'. The Northern Yuan page places both cities 'in present-day Inner Mongolia'. The spec is the same land as the Ming's ledger/11 gain of June 1370 (Inner Mongolia inside Cliopatria's 1375 Ming outline): 3,590 cells, about 908,000 km2 at 97.4-123.6 E. That is wide, since it reaches Alxa, but because it mirrors ledger/11 exactly the steppe now passes from the Yuan (September 1368) to the Northern Yuan to the Ming (June 1370) without an unheld gap. In the trial all 3,590 cells are taken from yuan-dynasty in 1368 and all go to the Ming in 1370.

The Hongwu page says Xu Da 'captured Taiyuan in January 1369, forcing Koke Temur to retreat to Gansu', and that in 1372 'Feng Sheng was assigned to conquer the western part of the Gansu Corridor' and completed the task. The region is the Gansu admin-1 (1,705 cells), the same as the Ming's ledger/15 gain of 1372, so there is no gap and no double claim. Two weaknesses, both covered by confidence 2: the same page has Koke Temur 'defeated in early May and fled to Karakorum' in 1370, so holding eastern Gansu in 1370-72 is a stretch; and the counterpart yuan-dynasty had ended in September 1368, so the trial takes the land from nobody. It is still better than the unheld gap it replaces.
